errors.text: The proposed compositions and initial structures do not reconstruct the sub-10 nm equiatomic AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles or their FCC multi-twinned/icosahedral morphology.
The intervention replaces rapid in situ vacuum heating to 973 K with 100–1000 hour annealing near 1273 K in argon, changing both the kinetic regime and dominant degradation processes.
The central claim of intrinsically sluggish diffusion directly contradicts the target finding of active, non-sluggish Au/Cu diffusion and surface segregation.
The proposed Laves/B2 precipitation and Zener-pinning mechanism is a bulk or micrometer-grained alloy mechanism, not supported for the target nanoparticles.

The predicted grain-growth plateau and persistent two-phase microstructure miss the observed loss of 2–4 nm particles, shape rounding, Au/Cu evaporation, distribution broadening, and approximately 22% size reduction.
The cited thermal evidence concerns a TiCoCrFeMn bulk alloy with micrometer-scale grains and cannot validate nanoparticle diffusion coefficients or stability.
Electrocatalytic dissolution evidence is not evidence for thermal diffusion or evaporation under vacuum.
